subject: Maths
subtopic: Sketching quadratic, cubic and reciprocal graphs
title: Sketching quadratic, cubic and reciprocal graphs
subtitle: Functions and Graphs · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can recognise and sketch quadratic, cubic and reciprocal graphs from their equations.

key_vocab.definition: A quadratic graph (y = ax² + bx + c) forms a U-shape (parabola). A cubic graph (y = ax³) has an S-shape. A reciprocal graph (y = &frac{a}{x}) has two separate curves.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can recognise and sketch quadratic, cubic and reciprocal graphs from their equations.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Types of graphs -- A quadratic graph (y = ax² + bx + c) forms a U-shape (parabola). A cubic graph (y = ax³) has an S-shape. A reciprocal graph (y = &frac{a}{x}) has two separate curves.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
The highest power of x tells you the shape: x² = parabola, x³ = cubic curve, &frac{1}{x} = reciprocal (hyperbola).
y = ax² + bx + c
a determines direction, c is the y-intercept

Key examples:
  ✓ y = x² is a U-shaped parabola  (minimum at origin)
  ✓ y = x³ passes through the origin with S-shape  (point of inflection)
  ✓ y = &frac{1}{x} has two branches in Q1 and Q3  (asymptotes at axes)
  ✗ y = x² is a straight line  (it is a curve)
  ✗ y = &frac{1}{x} crosses the y-axis  (undefined at x = 0)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – quadratic graph
  Sketch y = x² - 4
  Shape: U-shaped parabola (positive x²)
  y-intercept: when x = 0, y = -4
  x-intercepts: x² = 4, so x = 2 and x = -2
  U-shape crossing x-axis at (-2, 0) and (2, 0), vertex at (0, -4)
  (The -4 shifts the parabola down by 4 units.)

Example 2 – negative quadratic
  Sketch y = -x² + 9
  Shape: inverted U (negative x²)
  y-intercept: (0, 9)
  x-intercepts: x² = 9, so x = ±3
  Inverted U with maximum at (0, 9), crossing at (-3, 0) and (3, 0)
  (Negative coefficient of x² flips the parabola.)

sections.title: Identifying graph types
sections.content:
State whether each equation gives a quadratic, cubic, or reciprocal graph.

(a) y = 2x² + 1
(b) y = x³ - 3
(c) y = &frac{5}{x}
(d) y = -x² + 4x

sections.title: Key features of quadratics
sections.content:
Find the y-intercept and direction (U or inverted U).

(a) y = x² + 3
(b) y = -x² + 5
(c) y = 2x² - 8
(d) y = -3x²

sections.title: Finding x-intercepts
sections.content:
Find where each graph crosses the x-axis (set y = 0).

(a) y = x² - 9
(b) y = x² - 5x + 6
(c) y = x³ - 4x
(d) y = x² + 2x - 8

sections.title: Sketching from features
sections.content:
List the key features needed to sketch each graph.

(a) y = x² - 2x - 3
(b) y = x³
(c) y = &frac{2}{x}
(d) y = -x³

sections.title: Mixed graph problems
sections.content:
Answer each question about graphs.

(a) How many turning points does y = x³ - 3x have?
(b) What is the vertex of y = (x - 2)² + 1?
(c) Does y = &frac{1}{x} have any lines of symmetry?
(d) What happens to y = &frac{1}{x} as x gets very large?
(e) Vertex of y = x² - 6x + 8?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ y = x² + 1 never crosses the x-axis
✗ y = &frac{1}{x} passes through the origin
✓ A negative coefficient of x² flips the parabola upside down
✗ Cubic graphs always have three x-intercepts
✓ The y-intercept is found by setting x = 0

teacher_sections.title: Teacher Key & Mark Scheme
teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Identifying graph types:
  (a) Quadratic
  (b) Cubic
  (c) Reciprocal
  (d) Quadratic

Key features of quadratics:
  (a) y-int = 3, U-shape
  (b) y-int = 5, inverted U
  (c) y-int = -8, U-shape
  (d) y-int = 0, inverted U

Finding x-intercepts:
  (a) x = 3, x = -3
  (b) x = 2, x = 3
  (c) x = 0, x = 2, x = -2
  (d) x = 2, x = -4

Sketching from features:
  (a) U-shape, y-int = -3, roots at x = 3 and x = -1
  (b) S-curve through origin
  (c) Reciprocal, branches in Q1 and Q3, asymptotes at axes
  (d) Inverted S-curve through origin

Mixed graph problems:
  (a) 2
  (b) (2, 1)
  (c) Yes: y = x and y = -x
  (d) y approaches 0
  (e) (3, -1)
